title: Chinland Conflict Monitor
publisher: Chin Center for Peace and Reconciliation

incidents.text: Two men from Ngalhbual village were arrested and beaten by ZRA-EC troops stationed in the village under a curfew. One died on 6 February and the other on 8 February.
The junta carried out an aerial bombing of Matupi town. The extent of the damage was not known.
Two Myanmar men and one Myanmar woman were arrested at the border near Zothei village, Champhai District, with 945 grams of opium.

incidents.detail: Outpost of the People's Defense Army-Tedim
incidents.text: The Zomi Revolutionary Army (Eastern Command) launched an offensive against an outpost controlled by the People's Defense Army-Tedim, a member of the Chinland Council. Casualties not reported.

incidents.detail: General Administration Department office and police station
incidents.text: An aerial bombing at about 10:30 AM caused substantial damage to the General Administration Department office and the police station in Webula town.
Two 500-pound bombs were dropped on Sanpiah ward, Mindat town, at about 1:00 AM. Damage and casualties not reported.
An airstrike on Halta village at about 1:00 PM injured five civilians, including two children under ten, and destroyed three houses.
A bombing of Pyinwa village at about 9:00 PM destroyed a Presbyterian church and a community hall.

events.text: The Education Department of the Hakha Central Council said its schools had provided basic education to 22,487 students in Hakha Township between 2021 and 2024.

events.detail: Refugees from Sin Oe Wa village, Paletwa Township
events.text: Refugees from Sin-Oo-wah village, Paletwa Township, sheltering in Siaha District, Mizoram, reported growing pressure from an Arakan Army-appointed administrator to return home.
8,147 students were studying in 119 interim community-based schools in Paletwa Township, with 2024-2025 final exams scheduled for February, according to the Paletwa Township Council.

events.detail: Mindat, Kanpetlet, Matupi and Paletwa Townships
events.text: An outbreak of diarrhea and suspected cholera had affected 418 people in Mindat, Kanpetlet, Matupi and Paletwa Townships since late December 2024, with four deaths including three children under one year old.
At the Chinland Council's first-anniversary press conference, the Minister of Education said about 660 schools had been set up for the 2024-2025 academic year, serving more than 56,000 students.

events.others: Malaysia's special envoy for Myanmar (ASEAN chair 2025); KNU; KNPP
events.text: Malaysia's special envoy for Myanmar, representing the 2025 ASEAN chair, held meetings in Bangkok with the NUG, the K3C coalition (KNU, KNPP and CNF) and other stakeholders.

The Mindat Township People's Administration allowed residents to return to Mindat town only if they showed past contributions to the resistance or paid 500,000 MMK to the town fund. Many residents objected.
The Tedim Township Council completed road repairs in parts of Tedim Township, financed by local religious organizations.
The Hualngoram People's Organization announced that the Hualngoram region would be governed according to its traditional system from the pre-colonial and British colonial periods.
The CNF and nine other ethnic resistance organizations began drafting the Articles of Federal Transitional Arrangements (AFTA) for the transition to a federal system.

events.detail: Highways in the Hualngoram region and Thantlang Township
events.text: The Chinland Government and local administrations were jointly repairing major highways in the Hualngoram region and Thantlang Township.
A six-year-old child in rural Paletwa Township died for lack of medical treatment amid shortages of essential medicines.

events.detail: Eight villages on the Kalay-Gangaw road, southern Kalay Township, Sagaing Region
events.text: Junta airstrikes forced about 4,000 residents of eight villages along the Kalay-Gangaw road in southern Kalay Township, Sagaing Region, to flee. About 100 displaced people had diarrhea amid a shortage of medical supplies.
Avocado export prices from Chinland to Mizoram rose from 150,000 MMK to over 200,000 MMK per sack, according to local producers.
The Chinland Council distanced itself from the territorial dispute between the Chin Defense Force-Lautu and the Mara Defense Force and urged both to settle it through peaceful negotiation.

events.others: Mindat Township IDP Camp Management Committee
events.text: The Mindat Township IDP Camp Management Committee reported 226 cases of diarrhea across 13 villages in Mindat Township, with three deaths.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: The Government of India was preparing to suspend illegal trade at Border Trade Gate No. 2 between Champhai District, Mizoram, and Rihkhawdar town, according to the Times of India.
The CDF-Mindat ordered civilians in Mindat Township holding firearms, including M79 launchers and ammunition, to surrender them by 15 March.

After peace talks in Aizawl facilitated by a mediation group led by the Chief Minister of Mizoram, the Chinland Council and the Interim Chin National Consultative Council agreed to form a new council named the Chin National Council, with a Chin National Constitution Drafting Committee.

events.others: Mizoram Rajya Sabha MP K. Vanlalvena
events.text: Rajya Sabha MP K. Vanlalvena from Mizoram visited the CNF headquarters and met Chinland Council leaders.

events.detail: Paletwa public hospital and government offices
events.text: The Arakan Army was moving medical equipment and administrative resources from Paletwa public hospital and government offices to Rakhine State by military boat, raising concern about public services in the area.

incidents.actors: ZRA-EC vs CNA and People's Defense Army-Tedim
incidents.text: The Zomi Revolutionary Army (Eastern Command), which works with the junta, launched a surprise attack on the Chin National Army and the People's Defense Army-Tedim near Tunzan village. Casualties not reported.
The Mindat Township Administration reported clearing more than 2,000 landmines planted by junta forces while repairing roads and drinking water systems.
CDF-CDM Siyin, a Chinland Council member, announced coordinated action against opium cultivation, production and trade in areas it controls.

Although the junta had been absent for nearly three months, residents had not returned to Kanpetlet town because landmine clearance was still under way and the Arakan Army and CDF-Kanpetlet were present.

incidents.detail: Zamual village, two miles from Falam town on the Falam-Kalay highway (several villages share the name)
incidents.text: A junta airstrike at about 3:00 PM on Zamual village, two miles from Falam town on the Falam-Kalay highway, destroyed four houses.
A junta airstrike at about 1:00 AM on Tlangzar village on the Falam-Hakha highway destroyed four houses.
Junta artillery fired into Tedim Township at about 5:00 PM injured two civilians and damaged two houses.
The Chin resistance coalition seized most strategic positions of Infantry Battalion 268 in Falam. The battalion commander, a lieutenant colonel, was reported killed in action on 17 March.

incidents.actors: Lunglei District Special Branch and BSF
incidents.text: Four people from Myanmar and two Mizos were arrested in Lunglei with heroin worth about 800,000 Indian rupees. Weight not reported. Arrests counted: Myanmar nationals only.

incidents.actors: Anti-Narcotics Task Force, Saiha Youth Group and Bualpui NG YLA
incidents.text: A Myanmar national was arrested in Bualpui NG village, Lawngtlai District, with 5.5 kg of heroin valued at 1.5 million Indian rupees.

events.text: The CNF rejected the Ngawn Union Council's claim that the CNA financed or planned the formation of CDF-Ngawnngam, saying it does not interfere in local defence forces in areas free of junta control.
CDF-Thantlang Council said about 99% of Thantlang Township, except the town, ran under its local governance: schools up to Grade 12, health care for about 17,000 patients and 24 civil cases decided.
CDF-Thantlang banned hunting of wild animals, including muntjac and deer, in its areas from March to June 2025.
Only 471 students registered in Hakha and Tedim for the junta's 2024-2025 university entrance exams.

events.type: Alliance, merger or new body formed
events.others: Young Chin politicians allied with the junta (proposed Chinland New Congress party)
events.text: A group of young Chin politicians allied with the junta applied to the Election Commission to register a new party, the Chinland New Congress.
CDF-Thantlang issued fire prevention measures, asking residents to keep fire safety tools ready from 6 March to 3 May.

events.type: Public consultation or meeting with the public
events.detail: Daai region (Paletwa, Matupi, Kanpetlet and Mindat Townships)
events.text: The Daai Regional Council held a two-day education workshop with 120 representatives on interim education policy, plans for higher education and a unified regional curriculum.
In Paletwa Township, nurses and health workers were barred from treating patients or selling medicines without Arakan Army permission.
The Chinland Council held a political roadmap workshop in Chinlung town with 60 representatives of Chinland Council entities.
The Interim Khumi Affairs Consultative Council/Paletwa Council held its third assembly with 360 representatives and approved governance, defence and financial policies and operating guidelines.
The Mindat Township Administration reported repairing roads and drinking water systems in the township.
The Chief Minister of Mizoram acknowledged some benefits from ending the Free Movement Regime during the Mizoram Legislative Assembly session.
Clashes since 13 February and junta airstrikes in southern Kalay Township continued to displace civilians, who faced severe shortages of drinking water and food.
The Aizawl District Court notified that Myanmar refugees in Mizoram are not eligible for Indian documents such as voter ID, Aadhaar, birth, tribal or residential certificates.
The price of coffee in Tedim Township rose from 10,000 MMK per viss in 2024 to 15,000 MMK in 2025, according to local farmers.

events.type: Public consultation or meeting with the public
events.text: Leaders of the Chinland Council, Parliament and Government visited the Zophei, Mara and Lautu regions from 14 to 18 March to explain the newly enacted Chinland Local Administration Laws.
The CNF held the third Central Committee meeting of its 8th party congress on military, political and strategic policy, and reaffirmed its commitment to unifying Chin resistance groups.

events.others: Zo Reunification Organization (ZORO); India's Home Minister
events.text: The Zo Reunification Organization met India's Home Minister Amit Shah and urged him to reinstate the Free Movement Regime on the India-Myanmar border.

events.others: Farkawn Village Council and civil society organizations
events.text: The Village Council and civil society groups of Farkawn village, Champhai District, decided to close all market stalls run by Chin refugees by 31 May 2025.

events.type: Public consultation or meeting with the public
events.text: Chinland Council leaders visited the Matupi and Zotung regions from 17 to 21 March to consult communities on the new Chinland Local Administration Laws.
Mizoram's Home Minister told the Legislative Assembly the state was working with the central government to collect biometric data of more than 40,000 refugees, including 33,505 Myanmar nationals.
Commodity prices in Hakha rose sharply because of supply disruptions from Mandalay, causing hardship for residents.
Free anthrax vaccination for cattle, buffalo and other livestock began in Mindat Township, according to the Township Administration.

Health workers from the Chin Health Organization and the local administration vaccinated children under five in 65 villages of Paletwa Township (polio, rotavirus, measles-mumps-rubella, pentavalent and others).

On the 37th Chin Revolution Day the CNF announced the release of 72 prisoners, reported the capture of several junta bases in early 2025, and reaffirmed its aim of abolishing the 2008 Constitution and building a federal union.
CDF-Thantlang announced the confiscation of all assets in and around Thantlang town of a resident it accused of supporting the junta and aiding violent acts.
CDF-CDM Siyin banned vehicle movement in its area between 6:00 PM and 6:00 AM without prior notice, for security reasons.
CDF-Zotung urged residents not to carry weapons and required armed groups passing through the Zotung region to notify it in advance with identification.
About 3,000 residents of more than ten Asho Chin villages in the Ann-Padan area of Magway Region were displaced by junta airstrikes and ground offensives and needed food.
The CNF spokesperson dismissed the junta's NSPNC peace talks held in Naypyitaw on 24-26 March as deceptive and illegitimate because key stakeholders were excluded.

events.detail: Thanchaung-Kophe Gyi village, Daai Regional Council Area 2
events.text: A mother lost her baby in childbirth with no midwife or medical supplies in Thanchaung-Kophe Gyi village, Paletwa Township; she was taken to hospital in Mrauk U, Rakhine State.

events.detail: Response to the 28 March Sagaing earthquake
events.text: After the 7.7-magnitude earthquake near Sagaing on 28 March, the Chinland Council pledged 10 billion kyats, offered a free hospital and appealed for aid; the Chinland Government pledged medical supplies, food and reconstruction support.
The CNF urged the junta to stop airstrikes and military operations in earthquake-affected areas and to allow humanitarian access without political interference.
A spreading wildfire destroyed the houses of two displaced civilians at about 7:00 PM, according to local sources.

events.detail: Supply routes from Magway Region to Mindat and Matupi
events.text: The junta's Artillery Battalion 368 cut supply lines between southern Chinland and Magway Region, mainly affecting Mindat and Matupi Townships, and set up a new post near Pansan village, Kyaukhtu Township.

incidents.text: A junta aerial bombardment of Mindat town destroyed three civilian homes.

incidents.actors: Chinland Government forces and allies vs ZRA-EC
incidents.text: Chinland Government forces and allies fought defensive battles in and around Tonzang from 2 to 4 April against an offensive by the junta-allied ZRA (Eastern Command). CNF/CNA Brigade 4 and CDF-Hualngoram announced counter-attacks.
Junta fighter jets dropped two 500-pound bombs on Mindat town at about 1:30 PM, destroying five public buildings and damaging five civilian homes.
An afternoon junta airstrike on Kanpetlet town damaged 15 buildings, including five civilian homes, government offices, staff housing and a public hall.
ZRA (Eastern Command) forces burned down 75 houses in Nakzang village, forcing more than 410 civilians to flee to Tonzang town.
ZRA (Eastern Command) forces burned down 34 houses in Buangmual village while retreating from Chinland Government counter-attacks.

incidents.actors: Chin Brotherhood and allies vs junta (IB 268)
incidents.text: The Chin Brotherhood announced the complete capture of the Infantry Battalion 268 camp in Falam with allied forces, leaving Falam Township free of junta presence and seizing missiles, weapons, ammunition and cash.
A junta airstrike on Phui village at about 9:00 PM killed six civilians, including an infant and an Assemblies of God missionary, wounded nine and destroyed more than ten houses.
A junta airstrike on Saizang village at about midnight killed six civilians and injured one.
An airstrike near the Na-Ta-La school junction in Kanpetlet town at about 10:00 AM killed one civilian.

incidents.actors: Young Lai Association, Mizoram Police and Assam Rifles
incidents.text: A joint team of the Young Lai Association, Mizoram Police and Assam Rifles arrested a Myanmar national in Lungrang village, Hakha Township, near Siacangkawn village in Lawngtlai District, with 180,000 methamphetamine pills.
A junta airstrike at about 4:30 PM damaged Mindat Baptist Church (formerly Myoma Baptist Church) in Mindat town.
Junta airstrikes with two 250-pound bombs at about 5:20 PM damaged seven civilian homes in Mindat town.
Junta airstrikes on Matupi town and nearby areas at about 2:00 PM injured five civilians, including a pastor, and destroyed several homes.
On Easter Sunday at about 5:00 AM the junta-allied ZRA (Eastern Command) attacked Tonzang town, held by CDF-Tonzang, a Chinland Council member.
CDF-Hakha arrested two junta police officers who had threatened residents and extorted money at gunpoint in Hakha.
Junta airstrikes on Webula town at about 8:30 PM injured six civilians and damaged 15 buildings, including a church.

events.text: Over 100 of 270 displaced households from Paletwa Township relocated to Tuidan village, Lawngtlai District, faced severe food shortages and needed emergency help.
Charcoal prices in Hakha rose from 25,000 to 40,000 MMK per bag because of prolonged power cuts.
Indian government aid for earthquake victims arrived in Rihkhawdar, controlled by CDF-Hualngoram, for storage and distribution to affected areas.
More than 410 civilians from Nakzang village fled to Tonzang town after ZRA (Eastern Command) forces burned 75 houses.

events.others: Matupi Township Health Department; Chin Health Organization
events.text: The Matupi Township Health Department completed the first phase of vaccination for 40 children under two and 10 pregnant women, with support from the Chin Health Organization and donors.
The CNF rejected a Zomi Political Coordination Committee statement, saying the ZRA was trying to cover up its burning of Nakzang village and must take responsibility.

events.others: Chanmary Local Council; Young Mizo Association
events.text: The local council and Young Mizo Association in Chanmary ward, Aizawl, announced that displaced people from Myanmar may rent houses only with their consent and permission.
The Mizo Zirlai Pawl urged the Mizoram government to enact laws to support and protect displaced people.
The Chinland Council and the CNF congratulated the Chin Brotherhood and allies on capturing Falam town and pledged to keep fighting for a federal union and self-determination.
The Chin Refugee Committee-New Delhi asked UNHCR's protection unit to issue UN cards because of security concerns for displaced people from Myanmar in New Delhi.
The Mara Territorial Council/Mara Defense Force banned hunting, bird catching, killing wildlife, electric fishing and fishing with explosives in Mara territory from 16 April to the end of June.
CDF-Hakha called on all Chin youth to join the operation to capture Hakha, the capital of Chin State.
CDF-CDM Siyin arrested two men who had collected money from civilians in Tedim town by misusing the group's name.
The Lunglei District Superintendent of Police told displaced people at Nahasiha camp that they may not drive or own vehicles, on pain of legal action.
The CNF Working Group for Policy Studies held a two-day workshop on developing a gender policy in Chinlung, with about 50 participants including women party members and women soldiers.

incidents.text: CDF-Hakha arrested two junta-affiliated police officers who were posing as civilians to gather information on resistance forces.
A landmine explosion in Nga-lai village injured two civilians.
A junta airstrike on Mindat town killed civilians (number not reported) and damaged government buildings and homes.
Two junta strikes on Mindat town at about 10:30 PM damaged 15 civilian homes and public buildings, according to the Township Public Administration. Counted as one attack (same place, same time).
CDF-Hakha captured a junta soldier on 15 May; another soldier and a police officer defected on 15 and 17 May.

incidents.detail: Zong Taung village (not matched in MIMU)
incidents.text: A junta airstrike on Zong Taung village killed a student and a woman, injured 11 civilians and damaged a school and more than 40 homes.
A junta airstrike dropped two bombs on Tonzang town, injuring one civilian and destroying a government office and the Planning Department building.

HPO/CDF-Hualngoram arrested a school founder and Chin National Organization education board member in Ward 2, Rihkhawdar, with 427 small boxes of heroin; 6,000 amphetamine tablets, rupees and kyats from drug sales were also found. The Chin National Organization denied involvement.

incidents.detail: Near a captured former junta base, Shinletwa village
incidents.text: A landmine explosion near a captured former junta base in Shinletwa village at about 3:00 PM killed one person and injured another (civilian or combatant not stated).

incidents.detail: Advance from Kalay towards northern Chinland
incidents.actors: Chinland Council and Chin Brotherhood vs junta
incidents.text: The Chinland Council and Chin Brotherhood jointly launched a defensive operation against about 800 junta troops advancing from the base in Kalay towards northern Chinland, according to the CNF/CNA spokesperson.

events.text: The Mindat Township Public Administration banned hunting and capturing rare birds, including hornbills, during the May-June breeding season.
The Mizo Zirlai Pawl opposed the Indian government's border fencing plan, saying it would block the reunification of Chin (Zo) peoples.
The Interim Khumi Affairs Consultative Council and Paletwa Council held a public administration election and public meeting with over 70 representatives in the Sami region.
About 40 displaced people from Paletwa Township at Kheikhong village, Siaha District, were reported ill with diarrhea and malaria.
The Chin Health Organization announced that five students would be selected for scholarships to study nursing and laboratory science at an Indian university.

events.others: Young Mizo Association and three other civil society groups
events.text: Four civil society groups including the Young Mizo Association restricted the entry of new displaced people into Edenthar ward, Aizawl, except those already settled there.
The Chinland Council and Government held a completion ceremony on 6 May in Chinlung for medical interns and public health trainees trained under the Ministry of Sports and Health.
CDF-Thado and the junta-allied ZRA (Eastern Command) exchanged prisoners: four CDF-Thado members and one ZRA soldier were released.
India's central government and Mizoram's Home Department met online to discuss biometric data collection of displaced people from Myanmar in Mizoram, expected to start soon.

events.detail: Daai areas of Paletwa, Matupi, Kanpetlet and Mindat Townships
events.text: The Daai Regional Council announced that local governance and public administration had been set up in Daai areas of Paletwa, Matupi, Kanpetlet and Mindat Townships.
The Hualngoram People's Organization said the Hualngoram area, set up under the Chinland Constitution 2023, is under local administration and no longer part of any junta-designated township.
In Kheikhong village, Siaha District, 525 refugees from Paletwa Township (139 households) were suffering from diarrhea and malaria, with cases rising for lack of medicine.
The junta in Hakha blocked the Hakha-Falam and Hakha-Gangaw roads to restrict civilian movement, as defections to CDF-Hakha increased.

events.type: Road or trade route closed or reopened
events.text: The route between Lunglei District and Paletwa, used mainly to carry goods to Rakhine State, was closed on 16 May and reopened four days later.
The Electric Veng Local Council in Lunglei announced plans to temporarily hold the Myanmar ID cards of Chin displaced people living in its area.

events.detail: Twelve villages in Tat Chaung and Lan Dan village tracts
events.text: Twelve villages in the Tat Chaung and Landon village tracts, Paletwa Township, had a fever outbreak since March, with deaths reported for lack of medicine and health workers.

events.detail: Magway, Bago, Naypyitaw, Ayeyarwady, Yangon and Rakhine
events.text: The Asho Chin National Federal Council announced plans for self-determination and nation-building for Asho Chin people in 39 townships across six regions and states.

A meeting of the Peace Committee, CDF-Matupi Brigade 1 and Brigade 2 signed eight agreements, including not using arms to settle internal conflicts, free civilian movement and a new peacekeeping committee.
The Chinland Government's Ministry of Defence held a coordination meeting in Chinlung on training, formation and policy between the Chin National Army and local Chinland Defense Forces.

events.detail: Hmulpi, Htay Zang, Hein Zing and Bum Sam villages on the Kalay-Thaingin road
events.text: More than 1,300 people from four villages along the Kalay-Thaingin road had been sheltering in nearby villages and farms for about two weeks and needed food, shelter and medicine.

incidents.text: A junta airstrike dropped two bombs on Mindat town at about 6:00 PM, destroying a government building, according to the Township Public Administration.
CDF-Tonzang seized a base of the junta-allied ZRA (Eastern Command); two ZRA soldiers were killed and two drones, four weapons, a car and seven motorbikes were seized.

incidents.actors: Hualngoram Police and Hualngoram Reserve Force
incidents.text: During a security operation in Bethel ward, Rihkhawdar, Hualngoram Police and the Hualngoram Reserve Force arrested a man from Paltel village with about 270,000 stimulant tablets worth 56 million rupees.

incidents.actors: Chinland Council and Chin Brotherhood vs junta
incidents.text: A junta column moving from Kalay towards northern Chin State on the Kalay-Thaingin road was resisted by Chinland Council and Chin Brotherhood forces; ammunition was seized, some soldiers were arrested and some defected.
The junta bombed Lunghlaw village at about 9:00 PM. No damage was reported.
A man from Kalay Township involved in drug trading and use was arrested by the Central Young Lai Association in Thingkah village, Lawngtlai District, and expelled to Myanmar.
A junta airstrike on the Khaikam elephant camp at about 4:00 PM killed a 16-year-old boy and injured a woman.

incidents.detail: Laithan hill (Thangmaul), a public recreation site on the Kalay-Tedim road
incidents.text: The junta bombed Laithan hill, a public recreation site on the Kalay-Tedim road, at about 5:00 PM, injuring one local civilian.
Police on the Champhai-Aizawl highway arrested a woman from Tahan ward, Kalay, with 44 grams of heroin.
Indian authorities arrested a man from Tahan ward, Kalay, in Zokhawthar village with 142 grams of heroin worth over 400,000 rupees.

incidents.detail: Three junta outposts at Hmualpi, Siyin area
incidents.actors: Chinland Council and Chin Brotherhood vs junta
incidents.text: Chinland Council and Chin Brotherhood forces attacked three junta outposts at Hmualpi village from 26 June and captured them by 28 June; at least 15 junta soldiers died, according to local sources.
The junta dug up and destroyed part of the cross-border trade road between Tedim and Rih, making travel to the border difficult.
Mizoram Police and Assam Rifles arrested a Myanmar national in Zokhawthar with over 20,000 stimulant tablets worth 667,000 rupees, according to India Today. Reported in the July briefing.

events.text: Since April more than 100 residents in CDF-Asho-controlled areas of Magway Region had fever and seasonal flu, and urgent medical supplies were needed.

events.others: Zomi Federal Union Township Education Board
events.text: The Township Education Board of the Zomi Federal Union/PDF-Zoland warned it would act against officials supporting the junta, spreading hate speech or obstructing public education in Tedim Township.
The Mindat Township People's Administration said it was working to protect rare plants, wildlife and water resources, and planted trees at the town entrance for World Environment Day.
A house fire in Zaythit ward, Hakha, at about 11:30 PM killed a 35-year-old woman. The cause was unknown.

events.detail: Gangaw-Yezwa section of the Union Highway
events.text: The Chinland Government and the Zotung Federal Council were repairing rain damage on the Gangaw-Yezwa section of the Union Highway linking Magway Region and Chinland.
The Lautu People Affairs Council held its second regular meeting with 73 representatives and approved the 2025 Regional Municipal Law.
A junta offensive in northern Chinland had blocked the Kalay-Tedim road for nearly a month, cutting off goods and causing food shortages in Tedim Township.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: At the first Mizoram State Security Council meeting, Chief Minister Lalduhoma ordered stricter enforcement of the Inner Line Permit system amid concern about armed groups and drug trafficking from Myanmar.
CNF Vice Chairman Dr. Sui Khar told The Diplomat that junta airstrikes had worsened the humanitarian crisis and urged India to review its neutral policy on Myanmar.
The HPO Public Works Department banned large cargo trucks from main roads in the Hualngoram region from 15 June to 31 October to reduce rainy-season damage.

events.others: Elected MPs from the 2020 election; local administrations
events.text: The Chinland Council leadership committee discussed amending the 2023 Chinland Constitution, focused on establishing the Chin National Council; CNF representation was reduced from 27 to 15 members.
The ULA/AA designated Paletwa Township as one of eight districts of Rakhine State under its Arakan People's Revolutionary Government; the Global Khumi Organization strongly objected on 16 June.
The head of the Paletwa Council's Health Department reported malaria outbreaks in 65 villages under its control.

The Paletwa Council's Humanitarian Department gave 130 bags of rice and food to displaced Chin and flood-affected people in three villages of Lawngtlai District on 7-8 June, and 180 more bags of rice, 100 tarpaulins and 130 toilet pipes on 17 June.
The Chin Brotherhood spokesperson said all Chin alliance members consider Paletwa Township part of Chin State, not a district of Rakhine State.
The Lautu Region People's Administration banned extracting or trading rare orchids and required permits for collecting or trading tree roots and bulbs.

events.others: 18 armed groups under the Chinland Council
events.text: Eighteen armed groups under the Chinland Council urged all Chin forces to fight the common enemy, settle territorial and ethnic disputes politically after the revolution and not turn weapons on each other; the CNA spokesperson said the same.
The Paletwa Township Education Board appealed to donors for textbooks, stationery and furniture for community schools for the 2025-2026 academic year.

events.detail: Chin villages in Minbya Township, Rakhine State
events.text: Malaria outbreaks in Chin villages of Minbya Township, Rakhine State, had killed three people including a child since late May, for lack of medicine and health care.

The Central Young Mizo Association urged camp leaders, support groups and Chin parliamentarians to make refugees follow local rules, avoid drugs and crime, and apply for temporary residency cards rather than Indian citizenship documents.
On World Refugee Day the Chin Refugee Committee-New Delhi demonstrated at Jantar Mantar, calling on UNHCR to recognize displaced Myanmar nationals in India as refugees.
The Mindat Township People's Administration reopened the Mindat-Matupi road after repairing landslide damage.

events.others: Hakha Township Public Healthcare and IDPs Management Committee
events.text: Power cuts disrupted the oxygen plant at Agape Clinic in Hakha; a local health committee appealed for funds for a generator.
Mizoram's Home Department said biometric registration of over 30,000 people displaced from Myanmar in 11 districts would start in July.
Residents reported that the Arakan Army was restricting Starlink and internet use in Paletwa Township, causing an information blackout.

events.type: Public consultation or meeting with the public
events.text: The Mindat Township People's Administration invited public suggestions on the draft forest policy for Mindat Township.
Mizoram's Chief Minister told a Ministry of External Affairs official that strong action would be taken against displaced people from Myanmar who break Indian law.
The Zomi Federal Union/PDF-Zoland had been repairing landslide-damaged inter-village roads in Tedim Township for over a month.

incidents.actors: Maraland Defense Force and Arakan Army vs CDF-Mara
incidents.text: The CDF-Mara headquarters clashed with a column of about 100 troops from the Maraland Defense Force and its ally the Arakan Army, according to a CDF-Mara official.

incidents.actors: Chinland Council and Chin Brotherhood vs junta
incidents.text: Chinland Council and Chin Brotherhood forces retook positions at Mualpi village held by a junta column of about 800 troops; the junta lost many soldiers and retreated to Kalay, and weapons and ammunition were seized.
After fighting from 2 to 5 July, the Chin National Organization/Chin National Defense Force captured Rihkhawdar town, held by HPO/CDF-Hualngoram, including the CNA Brigade 4 headquarters.
The Chin National Army captured the CNO/CNDF headquarters; CNDF withdrew from Rihkhawdar after five days.

CDF-Hakha Central Council stopped two vehicles carrying about 3 million stimulant tablets and 110 kg of heroin; those involved carried a recommendation letter from a junta-aligned Battalion 15 commander in Yinmarbin. The drugs were burned.
Residents returning to Rihkhawdar after CNDF withdrew reported 13 homes burglarized and more than 21 motorcycles and cash missing.
The junta dropped a 500-pound bomb targeting the CDF-Matupi headquarters. No damage was reported.

incidents.actors: Narcotics Control Bureau and Assam Rifles
incidents.text: A joint NCB and Assam Rifles operation in Champhai District seized 642 grams of heroin and 10.44 kg of methamphetamine worth 367.9 million rupees. Suspects not reported.
Junta forces raided internet cafes run by Chinland Network and Shwe Hakha in Pyitawtha ward, Hakha, and confiscated their equipment.

The Hualngoram People's Organization burned 280,300 stimulant tablets, 430 packages of heroin and 4 units of crystal methamphetamine seized between 9 May and 9 June (not counted again as new seizures).
A landmine explosion in Mindat town injured two women; one lost a leg.

events.others: Interim Council of Myanmar Nursing and Midwifery Training School
events.text: The Chinland Government's Ministry of Health and Sport announced the second intake of a three-year Diploma in Nursing and Midwifery.
Mizoram's Home Department said biometric registration of over 32,000 Myanmar refugees in the state had begun.
CDF-Hakha/Hakha Central Council urged young men not to leave Hakha Township and called on youth abroad or elsewhere to return before the end of July for reserve military training.
The Chinland Council and the Chin Brotherhood separately urged HPO/CDF-Hualngoram and CNO/CNDF to seek peaceful dialogue; the fighting threatened the planned Chin National Council.
Fighting between CDF-Hualngoram and CNDF from 2 to 5 July drove over 3,000 civilians from Rihkhawdar and nearby villages to Zokhawthar, Mizoram. A woman drowned crossing the Tio River.

events.others: Advocacy Group for Peace led by the Mizoram Chief Minister's political adviser
events.text: An advocacy group for peace led by Pu Lalmuanpuia Punte, political adviser to Mizoram's Chief Minister, met HPO and CNDF leaders near the border and urged them to avoid irreparable mistakes and human rights violations.
The Paletwa Council said it would not support or join any Chin revolutionary group causing tribal or territorial conflict during the resistance.

About 500 refugees from Myanmar and Afghanistan protested at the UNHCR office in New Delhi from 7 July, led by the Chin Refugee Committee, demanding refugee status, refugee cards and protection; police tried to disperse the 17-day protest on 29 July.

events.others: National Unity Consultative Council; Acting President
events.text: The NUCC, the NUG and the Acting President separately urged Chin resistance forces to stop settling internal disputes by force and pursue political dialogue.

events.others: Chin Peace and Reconciliation Initiatives (Chin religious leaders, United States)
events.text: Chin religious leaders in the United States called on Chin resistance groups to stop hate speech and incitement online and avoid military solutions to internal conflicts.
CDF-Ngawnngam urged the Ngawn clan group not to get involved in conflicts related to CNO/CNDF and stressed Chin national unity.
India's Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways said the Kaladan project linking Sittwe and Paletwa would be fully operational by 2027.
The Chin Health Organization announced 18 scholarships for Chin students to study health courses (nursing, physiotherapy, prosthetics, X-ray and laboratory technology) at Indian universities.
The CNF/CNA said it had no intention of seizing townships already held by Chin revolutionary forces and would focus on protecting civilians.
The Chin Civil Movement called for an immediate end to armed approaches and for political dialogue among Chin revolutionary forces.
CDM health workers urged civilians to avoid hate speech, resistance groups to settle conflicts politically without disrupting public services, and media not to promote ethnic hatred.
Chin National University, under the Chinland Council and Ministry of Education, invited applications for over 20 academic posts.
The Lautu Region People's Administration confiscated and destroyed expired medicines and food in 18 villages, including Hnaring.

events.detail: From Para village, Mara region, to Siaha District, Mizoram
events.text: Construction began on a border road from Para village in the Mara region to Siaha District, Mizoram, led by the Maraland Territorial Council.

Mizoram Police and Assam Rifles arrested two local youths and the Vice Chairman of the Maraland Territorial Council in Tuipang for possessing weapons and ammunition; the Vice Chairman was released on 29 July.
Five groups (CDF-Zophei, CDF-Zotung, CDF-Lautu, CDF-Mara and Senthang Revolution Force, known as ZZLMS) urged that political differences be settled through dialogue, not arms.
The Chinland Council, Government and Ministry of Health and Sports advertised for three experienced nurse instructors for a new nursing school.
The Champhai sub-headquarters of the Young Mizo Association barred displaced people from Myanmar from forming separate churches or tribe-based religious organizations.
The CNF/A warned Chin revolutionary forces to beware of junta cyber warfare tactics and stay focused on revolutionary goals.
Biometric data collection for Myanmar refugees in Champhai town was set to begin on 31 July, according to the District Commissioner.

incidents.text: A junta airstrike on Mindat town at 8:50 AM damaged two government buildings and eight civilian homes, according to the Mindat Township Public Administration.
The junta arrested about 40 youths in Hakha, some returning from Sunday church service and others at a tea shop on the Hakha-Gangaw road; eight were later released.
HPO/CDF-Hualngoram detained the Assistant Executive Secretary-1 of CNO/CNDF at a military checkpoint; he was released on 24 August as a gesture towards peace.
At about 11:30 AM CDF-Hakha attacked a vehicle of a junta police territorial security unit at Thita junction, Hakha; one police officer was seriously injured and one member killed.
The junta arrested ten youths returning from church near Myoma market, Pyitawtha ward, Hakha.
A morning junta airstrike dropped two bombs on Kanpetlet town, damaging five civilian homes.

incidents.detail: Chyan Pyan village (not matched in MIMU)
incidents.text: An abandoned 60mm round exploded while children were playing near a house in Chyan Pyan village, injuring four children.
Junta forces opened fire near the clock tower in Hakha at about 11:30 AM, injuring a man and two female students; the man later died in hospital.

incidents.actors: Maraland Defense Force and Arakan Army vs CDF-Mara
incidents.text: About 200 troops from the Maraland Defense Force and the allied Arakan Army launched an offensive to seize the CDF-Mara headquarters; CDF-Mara told residents to avoid travel, not gather in groups of more than five and temporarily close schools.
At about 1:30 PM the junta dropped seven bombs on Mualbem and Zangzawl villages (recorded as one attack per village).
At about 1:30 PM the junta bombed Zangzawl village together with neighbouring Mualbem; one child from Zangzawl was injured.

events.text: The CNF/A and the Hualngoram People's Organization signed a five-point agreement on Chinland's liberation and building, including CNF/A taking charge of checks on Trade Route No. 2 at the India-Myanmar border.
The Zotung Federal Council issued transport rules banning loads above set weight limits on roads under repair in the Zotung region.

events.others: University of Medicine (1); Interim University Council
events.text: The Chinland Council, Government and Ministry of Health and Sports offered places to 30 students in the first MBBS program, with the University of Medicine (1) and the Interim University Council, starting January 2026.
UNHCR was to begin Refugee Status Determination interviews for Myanmar refugees in New Delhi from 8 August, according to the Chin Refugee Committee-New Delhi.
Chin Brotherhood representatives visited Laiza in late July at the invitation of the KIO/KIA and met its Deputy Chairman and senior NUG leaders.
The Tedim Township Council distributed rice for the second time to displaced people in villages across Tedim Township; no details were released.
The ULA/AA spokesperson announced that Paletwa Township, taken from the junta, was being made a district-level unit under AA administration.
About 2,000 Myanmar refugees in Mizoram had been registered in biometric data collection from late July to 11 August.

events.others: Chin Civic Movement; Global Khumi Youth Association
events.text: The Chin Civic Movement said the ULA/AA's unilateral incorporation of Paletwa into Rakhine State was unacceptable; the Global Khumi Organization and Global Khumi Youth Association said the Chin people of Paletwa do not accept it.
The CNA spokesperson warned that the ULA/AA running Paletwa as a district of Rakhine State without local consent could escalate the conflict.
The Tedim Township Public Administration arrested a merchant in a village with counterfeit 10,000-kyat notes worth over 100 million kyats.
The CNA spokesperson said it would not accept the junta's planned election (phase 1, 28 December) and would work to make it fail, warning supporters to reconsider.
The CNF/A rejected as baseless an India Tribune article alleging that the CNA supports drug traffickers, and asked for a review of its sources.
The Interim Chin National Consultative Council rejected the junta's election and urged international governments to oppose it.

events.others: ZZLMS coalition (CDF-Zotung, Zophei, Lautu, Mara and Senthang Revolution Force)
events.text: The ZZLMS coalition of five groups based in Hakha, Thantlang and Matupi Townships held its first joint military training.
The Chinland Council's 5/2025 meeting in Chinlung discussed 2025 financing, a committee to appoint leaders and restructuring the Chinland Government and its ministries.

events.others: Chinland Council, Chinland Government and Matupi Township Public Administration (accused)
events.text: MRO/CDF-Matupi condemned the forced conscription of youths, students and married men under 40 in its areas and in areas run by the Chinland Council and Matupi Township Public Administration, warning it could escalate conflict.
HPO/CDF-Hualngoram released the CNO/CNDF Assistant Executive Secretary-1, detained since 5 August, as a gesture towards peace.

Mizoram Police said 185 Myanmar nationals had been arrested for drug trafficking since 2021; a Special Drive on Drugs with the Central Young Mizo Association began field operations in border villages on 25 August.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: Mizoram's Home Minister told the Legislative Assembly that border fencing is a central government matter being carried out on its directions.

events.others: Chin Center for Peace and Reconciliation (CCPR)
events.text: CCPR published 'A New Front: Drug Trafficking Along the India-Myanmar Border', identifying Champhai District and Falam Township as main routes and about 2.7 tons of drugs seized between 2022 and July 2025.

incidents.detail: Laeshi village on the Mindat-Matupi road (not matched in MIMU)
incidents.text: A house break-in and killing took place in Laeshi village at about 11 AM; the suspect, from Saw Township, is being pursued, according to the Mindat Township Public Administration.
Two women from Seipui and Leilet villages, Falam Township, were arrested with heroin in Serchhip town at about 11 AM (amount not reported).

incidents.detail: Pangkhuar village, near the Tio River
incidents.text: A man from Salen village, Thantlang Township, was arrested with narcotics in Pangkhuar village; he tried to flee and drowned in the Tio River at the border.

incidents.detail: Kyan Thar village, southern Kalay Township
incidents.text: The junta launched a counter-offensive with about 200 troops to retake Kyan Thar village in southern Kalay Township, which CDF-Kalay-Kabaw-Gangaw had held; heavy fighting followed and the briefing summary reports the village was retaken.
At about noon the junta dropped three bombs on Khapan village, injuring one civilian.
Mizoram Police arrested a man from Khawmawi village, Falam Township, with 115 grams of heroin on the Champhai-Aizawl highway at about 9 PM.
A man from Kalay was arrested with 37 grams of heroin at a checkpoint between Champhai and Aizawl.
Mizoram Police seized 2.372 kg of methamphetamine tablets at the Tio River crossing; the suspect fled back into Myanmar.
At about 10 PM the junta air force dropped four bombs on two locations in Mindat town, damaging seven civilian homes. Counted as one attack (same town, same time).
A woman from Falam Township was arrested with 119 grams of heroin at a checkpoint in Champhai.
A woman from Falam Township was arrested with 127 grams of heroin in Zemabawk East ward, Aizawl.
At about 12:30 PM the junta dropped three 500-pound bombs on Paletwa town, killing two women, injuring 19 people and damaging public infrastructure. Counted as one attack.

events.others: Customs, narcotics control and the Central Young Lai Association
events.text: A four-month special operation by Mizoram police, customs, narcotics control and the Central Young Lai Association against drug trafficking from Myanmar began.
The Chinland Council and Ministry of Education announced that batch 2 of the Chin National University Pre-College Diploma Program would start in November 2025.

The junta filed a case at Hakha police station under its new election law against the Chinland Council Chairman, the Chinland Government Prime Minister and 16 Council members, accusing them of speeches and mobilisation to disrupt the election.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: Since August the Arakan Army has been issuing temporary border-crossing permits and controlling movement at the India-Myanmar border at Shinletwa village, Paletwa Township.
Robberies and threats on the Paletwa-Kyauktaw highway rose sharply, leaving Paletwa residents afraid to travel to Kyauktaw for health, social and economic needs.

events.detail: Htawhawi suspension bridge between Lautu and Mara regions
events.text: The Chinland Ministry of Construction and Lautu regional leaders inspected the rebuilding of the Htawhawi suspension bridge connecting the Lautu and Mara regions.

events.type: Harvest loss, crop pest or disease
events.text: Over 40 villages in Mindat Township reported widespread damage to crops, maize and vegetables from pests.
In Hriphi village, Thantlang Township, a displaced woman gave birth to triplets; the mother and all three babies died.
Residents were increasingly worried about the ULA/AA's August statement banning the entry of any other armed group.
A community-built school building in Ngalang village, Thantlang Township, collapsed in strong wind and heavy rain, disrupting classes.

events.detail: Four villages near the Mara conflict
events.text: With fighting ongoing since 18 July between the Maraland Defense Force with the Arakan Army and CDF-Mara, the Chinland Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs gave 100,000 MMK per household to displaced families from four villages.

MRO/CDF-Matupi ignored four requests for dialogue on the forced conscription of under-age students and education staff; the NUG Ministry of Education and Matupi Township Education Board urged it to respect the right to education.
The Mindat Township Public Administration completed a population census of more than half of Mindat Township to plan public services.
A seasonal fever outbreak in Mindat Township killed seven children under five in 2025, according to the Township Department of Health.

events.detail: Mindat, Matupi, Kanpetlet and Paletwa Townships
events.text: The junta's Union Election Commission announced that elections would not be held in 11 constituencies in Mindat, Matupi, Kanpetlet and Paletwa Townships.
Five children in the Daai region died of dengue between June and 15 September; medical supplies and health services were urgently needed.

events.detail: Road between Mindat and M'kuiimnu town
events.text: Landslides from continuous rain blocked the road between Mindat and M'kuiimnu town, disrupting the supply of essential goods.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: The Lawngtlai District Commissioner banned the export of chemical fertiliser to Myanmar for two months, citing its use in mining.
The Chinland Minister of Health said hospitals and clinics under the Ministry serve all Chin people regardless of political affiliation.
The People's Police Force under CDF-Kanpetlet told CDM police officers to join by the end of October or face consequences.

events.detail: Forest near Saikhumphai, close to Leilet village (Falam)
events.text: Assam Rifles found and seized a G3 rifle, a sniper rifle, a 60mm mortar and equipment in a forest near Saikhumphai, close to Leilet village in Falam Township.

On its fourth anniversary CDF-Daai restated its commitment to unite the Daai people under a federal state government, end military dictatorship and work with other Chin forces on nation and state building.
Assam Rifles and Mizoram Police arrested a Chin man with a rifle and ammunition in Zokhawthar, near border trade post No. 2.
The Chinland Ministry of Construction said the rain-damaged road between Thantlang town and the Zophei area had been repaired with local community leaders and reopened.

The Chin National University held its first pre-college diploma graduation: 140 students received a Diploma in Community Development, with the Parliament Speaker, Prime Minister and Education Minister attending.

incidents.detail: Eastern ward and a hotel in the western ward
incidents.text: At about 1:30 AM junta airstrikes hit a site in the eastern ward of Mindat town and a hotel in the western ward, injuring three civilians and damaging the hotel. Counted as one attack (same town, same time).
At about 7 PM a junta airstrike hit the Catholic church and school in Htin Chaung village, killing four students and injuring about 15 others; the buildings caught fire and collapsed.

incidents.detail: School in Vamthu village (not matched in MIMU)
incidents.text: At the same time as the Htin Chaung strike, the junta bombed the school in Vamthu village, damaging the building.
The junta bombed the area near the fire station in Matupi town at about 8 PM; residents reported deaths, injuries and damage (numbers not given).
Champhai District Police arrested two men, one from Khawthir village in Falam Township and one from Sagaing Region, with 1.627 kg of heroin on the Union highway.
At about 10:30 AM the junta bombed the school in Vanhar village, killing two students, injuring 21 others and badly damaging the school.

incidents.detail: Fire Station Hill and Khuavung ward
incidents.text: The junta air force bombed Fire Station Hill and Khuavung ward in Tonzang town, destroying three civilian homes.
At about 7 AM an airstrike hit the area near the General Public Hospital in Matupi town, damaging the hospital building.
CDF-Mara detained three CDM teachers from the Matupi Township Education Board, accusing them of refusing to support its draft local governance law.
Mizoram Police arrested a man from Ward 2, Rihkhawdar, in Zokhawthar with 1.215 kg of heroin.
CDF-Hakha attacked the Hakha town police station in the morning; five junta troops were killed and 15 detainees were freed.
The junta carried out an airstrike on a site in Matupi town at about 4 PM; no information on damage was released.
Assam Rifles seized 90 bags of poppy seeds and 120 bags of betel nuts smuggled from Myanmar near Ruangtlang village; the owner is unknown.

incidents.detail: Hmantaw village, southern Kalay Township; Kalay-Gangaw road
incidents.text: CDF-Kalay-Kabaw-Gangaw lost control of Hmantaw village in southern Kalay Township after a junta counter-offensive with a larger force; fighting continued along the Kalay-Gangaw road.
Four junta vehicles carrying troops advanced from Kalay towards Chinland on the Kalay-Tedim road in the evening, according to local sources.
At about 1 PM the junta bombed Zathal village in the Senthang area, damaging a school building and a home.

The junta dropped two bombs on a wedding ceremony of a CDF-Kanpetlet commander in Ward 2, Kanpetlet town, killing three men and one woman, injuring 15 others and destroying four homes. Recorded as a civilian area (a wedding).
The junta bombed Kanpetlet town at about 8:30 PM, damaging the fire station and three staff residences.
Local sources said the junta flew reinforcements 26 times by Mi-17 helicopter from Kalay to Infantry Battalion 269 in Tedim town between 26 and 29 October.
The junta carried out two aerial bombings on the Khonu Center in Mindat town on 26 and 27 October, damaging buildings; casualties were not known. Counted as two attacks (two days).

incidents.detail: Kyunchaung and Htukkyat villages near the Kalay-Gangaw road, southern Kalay Township
incidents.text: Over 100 junta troops raided Kyunchaung village near the Kalay-Gangaw road at about 1 PM and burned several homes; on 28 October they attacked Htukkyat village and burned houses.
About 100 troops from Infantry Battalion 269 advanced on the Tedim-Tonzang road towards Tonzang but turned back halfway the same day, according to the CDF-Tonzang commander.
At about 10 PM the junta bombed Taingen (Tai-ngin) village in the Siyin area, injuring a woman and destroying a home.
About 200 troops from Kalay and 200 from Tedim advanced on the Kalay-Dingin and Tedim-Dingin routes; fighting broke out with CDF-CDM Siyin near Mualpi (Hmualpi) village in the afternoon.

incidents.detail: About six miles outside Tedim on the Tedim-Dingin-Kalay road
incidents.text: About 200 junta troops advancing from Tedim on the Tedim-Dingin-Kalay road fought PDF-Zoland about six miles outside Tedim.

incidents.detail: Ha-Khalay village, Zanniatram area (not matched in MIMU)
incidents.text: Junta troops operating along the Kalay-Gangaw road entered Ha-Khalay village in the Zanniatram area of Falam Township and burned several homes.

events.others: ACR, CRC, Dai Community and FRO (Malaysia)
events.text: Four Malaysia-based Chin organisations held a two-day meeting with Chin leaders, pastors and community groups to coordinate support for Chin refugees in Malaysia.
Ten of the sixteen youths arrested by the junta in August while returning from church in Hakha were released.
Mizoram's Home Department said biometric registration of displaced people from Myanmar, begun in late July, was 37.4 percent complete.
A Chin resident of Daletza village, Paletwa Township, was released after more than two weeks in Arakan Army detention on accusations of leaking information about cross-border passports in Mizoram.

events.detail: 13 locations in Tedim and Mindat Townships and Mizoram
events.text: The Network for Chin Community Development distributed food to displaced Chin people at 13 locations in Tedim and Mindat Townships and Mizoram.

events.type: Public consultation or meeting with the public
events.text: A Chinland Council delegation led by its Vice President 2 with ministers made field visits and held public meetings in the Thado and Tonzang areas.
A coalition of 20 organisations including the CNF, NUG and KNU urged ASEAN not to recognise any junta-run election, to act to protect civilians and to demand the release of political prisoners.
Six ethnic armed organisations including the CNF urged the UN, ASEAN and diplomats not to attend the junta's 15 October ceremony for the 10th anniversary of the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement.

The CDF-Hakha Central Council condemned junta airstrikes on civilians, called for a full boycott of the election, warned of action against participants and urged international pressure to stop attacks.
The Chinland Ministry of Education condemned junta airstrikes on schools and schoolchildren and called for urgent international action.

events.detail: Gangaw-Aika and Hakha-Matupi routes, Zotung region
events.text: The Zotung Federal Council said heavy rain had caused severe landslides on the Gangaw-Aika and Hakha-Matupi roads, disrupting cargo, and that large funding is needed for repairs.
Assam Rifles arrested two men in Vaphai village near the border trying to smuggle explosives into Myanmar: 5,800 gelatin sticks, 10,500 metres of Cordtex fuse and 6,000 detonators.
The Chinland Ministry of Education announced three new faculties at Chin National University (Education, Law, and Technical and Vocational Studies) opening in January 2026.

events.detail: Villages near the Kalay-Tamu and Kalay-Gangaw roads
events.text: Over 10,000 civilians fled villages near the Kalay-Tamu and Kalay-Gangaw roads during large junta offensives and urgently needed food, according to the Kalay People's Defense Committee.

The Mindat Public Administration said vehicle owners who carried supplies for the resistance during the Mindat operation, and hold contribution certificates, are exempt from checkpoint taxes in the township.
On the 65th anniversary of the KIO/KIA the CNF reaffirmed shared goals with the Kachin, the NUG and other revolutionary forces.
Citing airstrikes on civilians and junta reinforcements for the election, the CDF-Hakha Central Council imposed a night curfew in Hakha.

events.detail: Motorcycle routes between Kalay and Tedim
events.text: Because of a large junta offensive on the Siyin area, CDF-CDM Siyin temporarily closed motorcycle routes between Kalay and Tedim.

The Chinland Council opposed the junta's December 2025 election, warned that participation by non-CDM civil servants would legitimise military rule, urged Chin people to stay away and asked the world not to recognise it.

events.others: Thantlang council Education Department; Senthang Central Council; Kanpetlet and Mindat Township Administrations
events.text: Because of continued airstrikes on schools, the Thantlang council's Education Department closed all community schools in its area indefinitely; Senthang Central Council and the Kanpetlet and Mindat administrations had done the same earlier in October.

incidents.text: The junta abducted 14 civilians from Suangpi village to serve as guides; they were rescued on 6 November.

incidents.detail: CDF-Hakha checkpoint on the Hakha-Matupi road
incidents.text: A junta column attacked a CDF-Hakha checkpoint near Loklung village on the Hakha-Matupi road, killing one resistance fighter.
Junta troops from Light Infantry Battalion 269 attacked along the Kalay-Taingen road and retook the Kennedy Mountain camp held by PDF-Zoland.

incidents.detail: Nat Chaung village, southern Kalay Township
incidents.text: In Nat Chaung village, southern Kalay Township, junta troops burned eight homes and killed two men, leaving their bodies in an irrigation canal.

incidents.detail: Kanparni camp on the Kalay-Gangaw road, southern Kalay Township
incidents.actors: Junta and Pyu Saw Htee militia vs Chinland Government forces
incidents.text: Fighting intensified as junta troops with Pyu Saw Htee militia launched a major offensive to retake Kanparni camp on the Kalay-Gangaw road, which Chin forces had taken in February 2025.

incidents.detail: Near Aa Lwe village (not matched in MIMU)
incidents.text: A junta column from LIB 269 clashed with PDF-Zoland near Aa Lwe village. Fourteen civilians from Suangpi village, abducted by the junta on 3 November to act as guides, were rescued; one woman among them was reported sexually assaulted by junta soldiers.
A village administrator in Paletwa Township, arrested by the Arakan Army on 26 October, was still held without family contact.

CDF-Hakha fired on four junta police officers in plain clothes who were extorting money in Myo Thit ward, killing one; junta troops then fired indiscriminately, injuring four civilians and burning one house.
Fighting at Taingen village between LIB 269 and CDF-CDM Siyin; over 20 junta soldiers were reported killed. Under heavy assault CDF-CDM Siyin left a junta camp it had captured.
At about 10 PM the junta dropped four bombs on Ruan village, damaging a religious building and a house.
PDF-Zoland announced it had retaken Kennedy Mountain camp on the Tedim-Taingen road.
At midnight junta airstrikes hit Thuklai (Htok Lai) village in the Siyin area, damaging religious buildings and a school.

incidents.actors: Chinland Council forces and allies vs junta
incidents.text: The Chinland Council and allies fought junta columns from Kalay; about 150 junta soldiers including officers were reported killed and weapons were seized.

incidents.detail: Aye Thayar village, mile 22 on the Mindat-Matupi road (not matched in MIMU)
incidents.text: At about 3 PM junta airstrikes hit Aye Thayar village, 22 miles along the Mindat-Matupi road, damaging homes.

incidents.detail: Near Taingen and in Falam Township, 26-27 November
incidents.text: Heavy fighting near Taingen in Tedim Township and in Falam Township on 26-27 November; six Chin resistance fighters were killed.
PDF-Zoland retook a junta-held position at Saimual hill near the 'Welcome to Tedim' sign, seizing weapons and capturing two soldiers.
At about 1 AM the junta carried out an airstrike on Ruan village, destroying four homes.

events.text: CDF-Asho said it gave medical care to 104 detainees and 127 civilians in Ngaphe Township, Magway Region, in October.
The Chinland Council issued eight prohibitions on taking part in the junta's election, including distributing pamphlets, and said violators would be penalised.
In Chaing Sa Nu village in the Daai area of Paletwa Township, a woman died in childbirth because no health care was available.

Diarrhoea broke out in early November in Karkhi and Twidan villages, Lawngtlai District, where many Paletwa refugees live: six deaths and about 54 cases by 12 November. About 300 people in the Shinletwa area of Paletwa were also affected.

events.type: Road or trade route closed or reopened
events.text: The Arakan Army closed border crossings between Mizoram and Paletwa during the diarrhoea outbreak.
The CNO/CNDF spokesperson said junta offensives in Falam Township had displaced over 20,000 civilians since late October, including 3,000 children under ten, who urgently need aid.
Mizoram authorities said biometric registration of over 31,000 displaced people from Myanmar was 58 percent complete.

events.type: Road or trade route closed or reopened
events.text: Mizoram reopened the Paletwa-Mizoram trade route after a two-week closure because of the diarrhoea outbreak.

incidents.text: A junta airstrike on Lumbang (Lungbang) village damaged four homes.
Mizoram Police arrested two Myanmar nationals and a local man with 5.935 kg of methamphetamine tablets and five packets of heroin.
Chin resistance forces intercepted a junta Y-12 aircraft supply drop near Lungbang and Varllon villages, seizing nine 60mm mortar shells and food.
A clash near Hlanzawl village killed three junta soldiers, including an officer, and one Chin resistance fighter.

incidents.detail: Route between Taingen and Zawngkawng villages, 4-19 March
incidents.text: Over 15 days CDF-CDM Siyin carried out repeated landmine attacks on a junta reinforcement column of more than 200 troops from Kalay, between Taingen and Zawngkawng; about 50 soldiers, including a colonel, were reported killed.
Junta troops deliberately burned Hlanzawl village; the extent of damage could not be confirmed because access was restricted.
CDF-Hakha targeted junta police officers who had been extorting money from civilians in Hakha; two were killed and one wounded.
A junta drone bomb attack on Lunghawh village killed a 19-year-old woman and seriously injured her mother.
Residents of Tuphei village found and cremated the body of an unidentified man buried in front of a house; junta troops are believed responsible.
Combined artillery and drone bomb attacks on Lungbang and Parte villages damaged one house. Counted as two attacks (two villages).
Chin resistance forces attacked junta troops collecting air-dropped rations in Falam Township, killing one soldier and wounding three.
A junta drone attack on Simzawl village killed a 56-year-old man and destroyed his house.

incidents.detail: Former LIB-304 camp and nearby areas, 11-13 March
incidents.text: Junta airstrikes hit the area around the former LIB-304 camp near Matupi town between 11 and 13 March, with four bombs in total. Counted as one attack because the briefing gives only the bomb total.
Unexploded ordnance found by children in Ramthlo village went off when handled, killing one child and injuring another.

incidents.detail: Near the Vaar bridge camp area
incidents.text: Junta airstrikes near the Vaar bridge camp area damaged several homes.
Airstrikes on Lunghawh village killed three civilians, including a child, and damaged four houses.
Eight fighters of the CNF-led joint forces were killed in the second week of sustained fighting in Falam Township.
Two bombs were dropped on Daidin village; no casualties were reported.
Three bombs were dropped on Matupi town; damage could not be confirmed.

incidents.detail: Chin State Parliament building and government offices
incidents.text: CDF-Hakha used suicide drones to attack the Chin State Parliament building and government offices in Hakha during a junta meeting.
CDF-Hakha condemned the junta for killing three men near Hakha Technology College and posing their bodies with rifles for propaganda.
Junta airstrikes on Zawngkawng village destroyed 14 homes.
Junta airstrikes on Kyaung Chaung village killed seven civilians, including four children, and injured four: the deadliest strike of the month.
CDF-CDM Siyin captured a junta soldier who had deserted his post near Zawngkawng.

incidents.detail: Near Mualpi village, on the way to road repairs
incidents.text: A 26-year-old woman was killed by a landmine near Mualpi village while going to help with road repairs.
Junta airstrikes destroyed the Rural Development office in Mindat; civilian casualties were reported but not confirmed.

events.text: The Thantlang Peng Council temporarily banned hunting or catching birds and animals in its area during the breeding season.
Mizoram's Home Minister warned displaced people living in the state against involvement in illegal activities.

The Lautu Region People's Administration required vehicle owners in the Lautu region, and outside owners bringing goods in, to register at its office; it also set rules on temporary household registration and visitor reporting.
The Zotung Regional Council's construction department began repairing the Rezua-Gangaw road with the Chinland Government, using two machines at an estimated 180 million kyats.
Assam Rifles and police arrested a man from Matupi in Siaha District with 19 air guns and related items.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: District administrations in Lawngtlai and Aizawl banned the illegal import, trade and storage of ginger from Myanmar (5-9 March).

events.detail: Displacement camps in Chinland and Sagaing
events.text: Women for Justice said displacement camps in Chinland and Sagaing urgently need medicine and supplies for women, including vitamins, contraceptives and hygiene products.
The Lautu Region People's Administration banned gambling in the Lautu region.
The NUG instructed allied organisations to get prior permission to move fuel through NUG-run areas when it is bound for Chinland, Kachin or Rakhine.

events.detail: Joint tax gates in Hakha Township and the Zotung region
events.text: The Chinland Government Prime Minister and cabinet members inspected joint tax collection gates in Hakha Township and the Zotung region from 10 to 12 March.
The Tonzang village youth group in Tedim Township banned opium cultivation in its area and warned of strict action.
CDF-Kalay-Kabaw-Gangaw held its Second General Conference from 11 to 13 March, reporting 92 members killed in the revolution and calling on all adults in its area to do military service.
Mizoram's Chief Minister said the state must engage the Arakan Army on the Kaladan project because the AA now controls Paletwa Township.
CDF-Hakha publicly apologised to 16 youths after confirming its members had beaten them at a checkpoint on 7 March.
The Chinland Council announced a minimum three-year military service policy so that areas taken from the junta are not lost again.
The CNF sent a message of support to the CRPH for holding its ninth parliamentary session.
Mizoram's Governor said there are plans to extend the Mizoram railway to the border to link with the Kaladan project.

The first draft-law committee meeting of the Chinland Council's second term, in Chinlung, discussed the Chinland Export and Import Draft Law. The Council also set public holidays under the Chinland Constitution (2023).
On the 38th Chin Revolution Day the CNF called on Chin adults to serve the revolution and warned against the junta's planned election.
The CNF granted amnesty to 30 prisoners of war.
CHRO condemned the appointment of two junta officers accused of human rights violations as military representatives in the Chin State Parliament.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: Siaha District imposed a two-month ban on the illegal export of fuel to Myanmar to prevent local shortages.
The ICNCC/CB Chairman said Chin armed groups would work towards unity once the junta is driven out, calling the Falam battle a shared struggle.
A village meeting in Valvum banned opium cultivation; violators face expulsion and confiscation of property.

events.detail: Displacement camps at the India-Myanmar border, Paletwa region
events.text: Chinland Council and Government officials visited displacement camps on the border in the Paletwa region from 23 to 26 March, delivering aid and discussing education and health care.

actors: Chinland Govt: Ministry of Home Affairs
events.others: Chinland People's Police; local police forces
events.text: The Chinland Ministry of Home Affairs held the first coordination meeting between the Chinland People's Police and local police forces on public security and the rule of law.

events.others: Chin Center for Peace and Reconciliation (CCPR)
events.text: CCPR reported distributing 2,426 bags of rice to 7,277 displaced people in five townships between October 2025 and March 2026.
The CNO/CNDF condemned opium cultivation in Falam Township and warned of prison or fines.

events.type: Alliance, merger or new body formed
events.text: The Steering Council for the Emergence of a Federal Democratic Union (SCEF) was formed by the CNF, KIO, KNU, KNPP, NUG and CRPH to coordinate the revolution and the transition to a federal democratic union.

events.type: Meeting or agreement between border authorities
events.text: Chinland Council and Government officials met the MZP and ZORO in Aizawl on aid for displaced people and university access for displaced students in Mizoram.

events.detail: 30 villages in Falam and Tedim Townships
events.text: More than 3,000 people from 30 villages in Falam and Tedim Townships had been displaced for over four months, short of food, shelter, sanitary supplies and medicine, with little aid access.
Fuel shortages worsened across Chinland, with petrol above 40,000 kyats a gallon in some areas.

Demand for avocado and grapes from northern Chinland fell sharply; ginger and chilli farmers in central Chinland were hit by Mizoram's crackdown on cross-border trade; southern farmers sold crops cheaply because of checkpoints and levies on routes to Magway.

incidents.text: At about 3:20 PM the junta dropped two 500-pound bombs on Khuapisip (Khawpichip) village, killing seven civilians including three children, wounding nine and damaging over 10 homes.
A junta drone bomb hit civilians sheltering in farm huts near Thlanrawn village, killing a 17-year-old girl from Arva village.

incidents.detail: Near Leithingkung (not matched in MIMU), 2-4 May
incidents.text: Heavy fighting near Leithingkung between Chin Brotherhood forces and a junta column marching from Kalay to reinforce Tedim town, with casualties on both sides.

incidents.detail: Fuel station at the town entrance
incidents.text: A 13-year-old was killed when an artillery shell fired by LIB 269 in Tedim town exploded at a fuel station at the town entrance.
CDF-CDM Siyin ambushed a junta supply convoy from Kalay with landmines near Hiangzing (Heinzin) village, causing 13 junta casualties and seizing three small arms.

incidents.detail: Kennedy Peak outpost near Tedim town
incidents.text: On 5-6 May the junta retook the Kennedy Peak outpost near Tedim town with superior ground and air forces; Chin Brotherhood forces withdrew.
At about 4 PM the junta dropped three drone bombs on Phunom village, killing three civilians, injuring one and destroying an Assemblies of God church.
The CNA fought a junta column of about 300 advancing from Falam town on the Falam-Hakha highway; 15 junta soldiers were killed.
A junta column of about 600 from Kalay reached Light Infantry Battalion 269 in Tedim town as reinforcements, according to local sources.
At about 7 AM a junta jet dropped four bombs on Mindat town, damaging the immigration and national registration office and the fire station.

Nine junta airstrikes on three locations in Mindat town on 11-12 May killed four people, including prisoners of war, wounded several and destroyed 15 homes, 10 government buildings and 4 vehicles. Counted as nine attacks, as reported.
Champhai District Police arrested a man from Chinland with over 10.8 kg of stimulant tablets and 75 grams of heroin.
The CDF-Hakha Central Council detained a member of the junta-backed Pyu Saw Htee militia in Hakha town for extortion and threats.

incidents.actors: Junta and ZRA-EC vs Chin resistance forces
incidents.text: Heavy fighting near Tonzang town as a joint column of over 800 junta and ZRA (Eastern Command) troops tried to retake the town.

incidents.detail: Towns in Mindat, Kanpetlet and Matupi Townships, 13-22 May
incidents.text: Over 10 days the junta carried out 25 aerial bombings on towns in Mindat, Kanpetlet and Matupi Townships, killing two civilians including a newborn, injuring several and destroying homes, shops and government offices. Counted as 25 attacks, as reported; the briefing does not split them by township, so they are placed in Mindat Township.
A CNA-led force ambushed a junta column carrying the LIB 266 commanding officer near the six-way junction in Hakha; four junta soldiers were killed and many, including the commander, wounded.

incidents.detail: Tedim-Tonzang road, Cikha-Tonzang road and village roads
incidents.text: Junta and ZRA forces launched a three-pronged offensive on Tonzang along the Tedim-Tonzang and Cikha-Tonzang roads and village roads.
At about 5:30 PM the junta carried out two aerial bombings on Lungzan village; casualties and damage could not be verified. Counted as two attacks.
The junta carried out an airstrike on Tonzang town in the afternoon, during fighting for the town; no details were given.

incidents.detail: Between Tonzang town and Tungtuang village
incidents.actors: Chinland Council forces vs junta and ZRA-EC
incidents.text: Fierce fighting between Chinland Council forces and the junta-ZRA column between Tonzang town and Tungtuang village.

incidents.actors: Central Anti-Drug Squad and Central Young Mizo Association
incidents.text: The Central Anti-Drug Squad and Central Young Mizo Association arrested a Myanmar national in Aizawl with 20 packets of heroin.

incidents.actors: Junta and ZRA-EC vs Chinland Council forces
incidents.text: After sustained air and artillery bombardment, junta and ZRA forces gained control and Chinland Council troops withdrew from Tonzang town.
Five days of heavy fighting at mile 6 near Kanpetlet town between Chin resistance forces and a junta column advancing from Saw Township.
Police in Zokhawthar arrested a man from Tedim Township with three soap cases of heroin.
Police in Zokhawthar arrested a woman from Khawmawi village, Falam Township, with 1.66 kg of heroin.
Champhai District Police stopped a vehicle and arrested two residents and a Myanmar national with 9.5 kg of stimulant tablets.

events.detail: 10 sites in Chin State, Sagaing and Mizoram
events.text: The Network for Chin Community Development gave food to displaced Chin people at 10 sites in Chin State, Sagaing Region and Mizoram (4-17 May).
Assam Rifles found a 60mm mortar tube, mortar shells, grenades, radios and IEDs hidden in a forest near the border in Champhai District.
After the junta retook Falam and with rumours of an attack on Rihkhawdar, over 820 displaced people from Falam Township crossed into Zokhawthar, Mizoram.
The Maraland Administrative Council banned chemical pesticides, herbicides and similar toxic substances in Maraland, citing risks to health, soil, water, livestock and the environment.
The CNDF and CDF-Thantlang held graduation ceremonies for military trainees and reserve forces.

The Narcotics Control Bureau arrested in New Delhi a man it described as a major coordinator of drug trafficking from Myanmar into Mizoram, Manipur, Assam and Tripura. In May Mizoram law enforcement arrested five people from Chinland, seizing about 12.07 kg of heroin and 20.318 kg of other drugs.

events.type: Public consultation or meeting with the public
events.detail: Lautu, Mara, Thantlang and Zophei regions
events.text: Chinland Government ministers visited the Lautu, Mara, Thantlang and Zophei regions from 18 to 22 May, meeting local officials and residents on health, education and humanitarian services.

The Chin People's Union appealed to Chin diaspora communities for defence funding as the junta prepared offensives in southern Chin State; on 25 May it asked for tens of billions of kyats for counter-offensives in southern Chinland and the Yaw region.
Citing security operations, CDF-Hualngoram restricted travel hours on the Laitui-Rihkhawdar highway.

events.type: Order or policy by border authority
events.text: The Lawngtlai Deputy Commissioner's office issued strict controls on illegal fuel sales and smuggling into Myanmar.
Fearing junta infiltration, the Senthang Central Council required travel recommendation letters and urged residents to prepare bomb shelters and stock supplies.
